summary: High 5xx saturation observed during tenant priority matrix reshuffle causing runtime restarts and elevated latency
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled tenant priority matrix reshuffle, ClearStream observed a sudden and sustained increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API.
Impact: Customer requests (chat + embeddings) saw 15-25% error rates and 3x p95 latency for ~45 minutes, causing degraded UX and automated retries.
Environment: prod, us-east (dedicated pool for ClearStream).
Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger tenant priority reshuffle (internal). 2) Simulate steady ~200 rps small payload chat + embedding mix. 3) Observe API 5xx rate and runtime restarts.
Observed logs/metrics: apigw: 502/503 spikes mapped to elevated upstream errors; runtime: repeated worker processes exiting with SIGABRT; scheduler: rapid preempt/reassign events; autoscaler: transient scale-down followed by scale-up.
Initial customer report: "Starting ~13:10 UTC our integration began returning server errors for short requests and retries compounded errors. This lasted ~40m and then dropped."
comments: Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-13T13:22Z: Acknowledged. Gathering traces and escalating to SRE. Opening this ticket to track customer impact.
SRE (Mateo Ruiz) 2026-03-13T13:31Z: Observed accept-queue growth on edge nodes handling ClearStream tenant. Confirming correlated runtime exits and increased preempt events. Collecting core dumps.
Customer (ClearStream - Jordan Lee) 2026-03-13T13:45Z: We saw embed + chat calls failing with 502; SDK retries made things worse. Happy to provide request IDs, sent via original support email.

SRE (Mateo Ruiz) 2026-03-13T14:10Z: Hypothesis: priority reshuffle triggered aggressive reassign of tenant affinity leading to connection churn and runtime worker thrash; autoscaler briefly scaled down due to mis-evaluated utilization causing GPU warmup latency and watchdog-triggered exits.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-13T14:50Z: Provided workaround to customer: pause reshuffle or throttle tenant migration window; ClearStream paused migration at 14:37 UTC and error rate dropped.
SRE (Mateo Ruiz) 2026-03-14T09:12Z: Added temporary guard in scheduler to delay affinity shifts if accept-queue > threshold. Preparing PR for durable fix.
investigation_notes: 13:25 UTC - accept queue for tenant-specific edge pool increased from baseline 50->600 connections.
13:27 UTC - several runtime workers OOM-like exits; kernel logs show SIGABRT in nvml driver calls in some cores.
13:32 UTC - autoscaler observed drop in utilization (due to preempted workers) and signaled scale-down; subsequent scale-up introduced warmup latency and increased hedged retries.
Hypothesis A: rapid tenant migration caused connection handoff race between apigw and runtime proxies leading to conn resets and watchdog restarts.
Hypothesis B: GPU driver faults triggered worker exits coincident with high connection churn; need to correlate NVML driver logs with kernel dumps.
Correlated traces: requestIDs 9c7f-xxxx, 9c8a-xxxx show API gateway returned 502 immediately after proxy handshake failure.
Related runbooks: tenant migration (confluence link) and runtime crash triage.
resolution: Workaround: Customer paused priority matrix reshuffle which immediately reduced error rate. Temporary mitigation applied: scheduler guard to prevent affinity reshuffle when accept-queue > 200 connections and delay autoscaler scale-down for 2 minutes after migration events. Long-term fix: patch scheduler to perform staged handoffs with connection draining control and improve autoscaler heuristics to avoid reactive scale-down during migration. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1295. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and add migration canary tests. Ticket will be updated when PR is merged and deployed.
